clue.text: Got the best of the stuff

definitions.meaning: to get the better of an opponent is to beat them, an old verb sense
stuff here is cloth or fabric, specifically a smooth woollen yarn and cloth

explanation.definitionFit: To worst someone is to defeat them, and the past form doubles as the name of a fine woollen fabric.

clue.text: An emblem otherwise represented

indicators.note: read as re-presented, the word otherwise is presented again in a new order

explanation.surface: A symbol depicted in some different way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented' signals the anagram: OTHERWISE rearranged gives the answer. The WHITE ROSE is the emblem of Yorkshire and of the House of York.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale bloom of this kind is the heraldic badge of the House of York and of Yorkshire.

clue.text: Instrument about to become the title of a book

parts.note: a rebec is a medieval bowed stringed instrument
CA is circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A musical instrument is about to lend its name to a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The book is Daphne du Maurier's 1938 novel. 'to become' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Daphne du Maurier's famous novel bears this woman's name as its title.

clue.text: I got supplanted by Miss Doolittle in third place on the coast

indicators.note: to be supplanted is to be pushed out and replaced, so the letter I is swapped for the name

parts.note: third is abbreviated in its ordinal form
Eliza Doolittle is the flower girl in Shaw's Pygmalion and My Fair Lady

explanation.surface: Eliza Doolittle elbows the narrator out of third spot somewhere on the shore.
explanation.walkthrough: In 3RD written as THIRD, the I is replaced by ELIZA to give TH+ELIZA+RD. 'got supplanted by' signals the swap. THE LIZARD is the headland in Cornwall that is mainland Britain's southernmost point.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lizard peninsula in Cornwall is a headland on the English seaboard.

clue.text: Wet right in the swim

indicators.note: the letter for right goes into the word for a swim

parts.note: a dip is a short swim

explanation.surface: Someone soaked through after a dip in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wet' looks like an adjective about swimming, but it is the noun sense: a feeble, ineffectual person, which in British slang is a drip.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses both words for a weak, spineless person lacking any spirit.

clue.text: Exponents of batting got a century in a day in olden times

parts.note: in cricket the side batting is in

indicators.note: the letter for a hundred is placed inside the Latin word for a day

parts.note: dies is Latin for day, the language of ancient times
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Records from a cricket innings long ago when someone made a hundred in a day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exponents' looks like players, but it is the mathematical sense: powers. A cricket side batting is said to be in; DIES is Latin, the tongue of olden times.
explanation.definitionFit: In algebra the small raised numbers showing powers are also called by this plural.

clue.text: I had invested in friendly cow

indicators.note: to be invested in something is to be placed within it, so the short form goes inside

parts.note: intimate means close and friendly
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone has put money into an affectionate farm animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cow' looks like the animal but is the verb: to frighten someone into submission.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow somebody is to browbeat or frighten them into obedience.

clue.text: After murder head of gendarmerie becomes active

indicators.note: the leading letter comes after the phrase for murder

parts.note: to do in is slang for murder

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of gendarmerie

explanation.surface: A French police chief springs into action after a killing.
explanation.walkthrough: DO IN is slang for kill; G, the head of 'gendarmerie', follows it. 'becomes' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone up and doing is busy and occupied, which is to be energetic.

clue.text: Fool providing a daily story

parts.note: a daily or char is a British cleaning woman who comes in each day
a story is a lie, as in telling stories

explanation.surface: A clown supplying the newspaper's front-page tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a daily' suggests a newspaper, but it is a CHAR, a British cleaning lady. A charlie is British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a proper charlie is a silly person or idiot.

clue.text: Guide to cheapest accommodation when short of time

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so the word for time is removed

parts.note: steerage was the cheapest passenger class on a ship
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A guidebook to budget lodgings for a traveller in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guide' looks like a book, but it is the verb. STEERAGE less AGE leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To steer is to direct a course, which is to lead or pilot.

clue.text: Fill one with honour outside that all may see

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the honour goes outside the film rating letter, enclosing it

parts.note: the MBE, Member of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing, suitable for everyone

explanation.surface: Someone stuffed with public honours for all to witness.
explanation.walkthrough: MBE is a British honour; the U certificate marks a British film anyone may watch. 'outside' puts MBE round U.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbue is to saturate or permeate something thoroughly, as a dye does.

clue.text: I interact with difficulty — I'm involved

indicators.note: the letters can be fitted together only with difficulty, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone socialises awkwardly and admits being mixed up in things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm' lets the answer speak for itself; the definition is 'involved', in its sense of complicated.
explanation.definitionFit: Something involved is complex, full of tangled detail and hard to follow.

clue.text: Master of elementary mathematics

parts.note: elementary is a pun on the Elements, the Greek geometry treatise, so the master is its ancient author rather than a schoolteacher

explanation.definitionFit: The Greek geometer wrote the Elements, the foundational textbook of geometry.

clue.text: Runner more complacent about start of lap

indicators.note: about means going round, so the comparative surrounds the letter

parts.note: smugger means more self-satisfied

indicators.note: start of means the first letter of lap

explanation.surface: A self-satisfied athlete at the beginning of a circuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete, but it means someone who runs contraband. 'about' puts SMUGGER round L.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner of contraband, such as a rum-runner, carries illegal goods past customs.

clue.text: Writer takes a month to cover riotous revels

indicators.note: to cover is to enclose, so the month wraps round the scrambled word

parts.note: June is a month

indicators.note: riotous means wild and disorderly, so the letters of revels are rearranged

explanation.surface: A journalist reports on a month of wild parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riotous' rearranges REVELS into LESVER, and 'to cover' wraps the month round it. Jules Verne is the French author of adventure novels.
explanation.definitionFit: The French novelist wrote Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea and other adventures.

clue.text: Jack Tar, also known as Port

parts.note: a Jack Tar is a sailor; OS is an ordinary seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor with an alias registered at his home harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: OSAKA is a major Japanese port city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese city is a major harbour on the bay of the same name.

clue.text: Submarine left to provide protection on the bottom

parts.note: submarine as an adjective means beneath the sea

explanation.surface: A submarine sets off to guard the seabed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Submarine' looks like a noun, but it is the adjective meaning below the sea. The answer is the protective coating sprayed on a car's underside.
explanation.definitionFit: This tarry coating is sprayed under a vehicle's floor to prevent rust.

clue.text: Expression of disapproval in file on Mr Pleydell

indicators.note: in a down answer, on means the second piece is placed after the first

parts.note: a rasp is a coarse file
Bertram Pleydell, called Berry, is the hero of Dornford Yates's Berry and Co. stories

explanation.surface: A complaint lodged on the dossier about a certain gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'file' looks like a dossier, but it is the tool, a RASP. Berry is Bertram Pleydell from Dornford Yates's stories. A raspberry is a rude noise of contempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Blowing a raspberry is a rude spluttering noise made to show contempt.

clue.text: A girl they moved a very long way

indicators.note: moved means shifted about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A young woman and her family relocated a great distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' signals the anagram of A GIRL THEY. A light-year is the distance light travels in a year.
explanation.definitionFit: This astronomical unit is the vast distance light covers in twelve months.

clue.text: Suitable means of attaining one's end

definitions.meaning: as an adjective, convenient and advantageous for a purpose
as a noun, a device or measure used to achieve something

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means advisable or convenient; as a noun it is a device used to achieve a goal.

clue.text: Dog after another animal in the queue

indicators.note: the word for dog comes after the animal

parts.note: a pig is an animal
to dog someone is to tail them

explanation.surface: A dog trails behind another animal in the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog' is the verb, to follow, giving TAIL. 'queue' is not a line of people but the old word for a plait of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A queue is an old word for a plait of hair hanging down the back.

clue.text: Rock music

definitions.meaning: to rock is to sway back and forth
a style of big-band jazz from the 1930s and 1940s

explanation.definitionFit: To sway to and fro is to oscillate; the word also names big-band jazz.

clue.text: Estimated bill I then received

indicators.note: to receive is to take in, so the word for then holds the abbreviation

parts.note: next means then, afterwards
AC, account, is a bill

explanation.surface: Someone gets a rough bill and pays it later.
explanation.walkthrough: AC is the abbreviation of account, a bill. 'received' puts it inside NEXT.
explanation.definitionFit: An estimated figure is approximate, not precise.

clue.text: "Minus ten' I gave out

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to a score of minus ten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' signals the anagram of TEN I GAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A negative number is below zero, shown with the subtraction sign.

clue.text: Your uncle — an upright and wealthy man

indicators.note: in a down answer, upright means the run of letters is read from the bottom up

parts.note: from the phrase Bob's your uncle

explanation.surface: A rich and honest uncle.
explanation.walkthrough: BOB comes from the British phrase 'Bob's your uncle', meaning that's all there is to it. 'upright' turns BOBAN into NABOB.
explanation.definitionFit: A nabob was a European grown rich in India, hence any very rich man.

clue.text: Initially, take a sample to eat

definitions.text: Initially, take a sample to eat

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Advice to try a little food before eating.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters of TAKE A SAMPLE TO EAT spell the answer, and the whole clue also defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: To try a small bit of food is to sample its flavour.

clue.text: Express disapproval in the end

definitions.meaning: to protest or raise an objection
the end means a goal or aim

explanation.definitionFit: To protest is the verb sense; as a noun the word means purpose or goal.

clue.text: Hijack reported by witnesses

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the word is said aloud

parts.note: to hijack is to seize

explanation.surface: A hijacking described by bystanders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'witnesses' is the verb: someone who witnesses an event observes it.
explanation.definitionFit: To witness something is to observe it with one's own eyes.

clue.text: Restaurant about to be incorporated in golf club

indicators.note: incorporated in means taken into the body of, so the short word goes inside

parts.note: a brassie is an old wooden golf club, roughly a two-wood
about is usually RE, as in regarding; here it must enter the club with its two letters swapped

explanation.surface: A restaurant is about to be set up within a golf clubhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'golf club' suggests a clubhouse, but it is the BRASSIE, an old wooden club. The usual RE for 'about' must go in as ER (BRASS-ER-IE), an irregularity the clue does not signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A brasserie is an informal French-style eating place.

clue.text: What to do, we hear, with this 7's work

definitions.text: What to do, we hear, with this 7's work

indicators.note: we hear means the word is spoken, so it sounds like the entry

parts.note: what one does with a book is to read it

explanation.surface: A question of what to make of a certain Charlie's writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 is CHARLIE, so 'this 7' is Charles Reade, the Victorian novelist of The Cloister and the Hearth; what you do with his work sounds like his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Reade was a Victorian novelist, so his books are there to be read.

clue.text: Hold meeting about the backing of film

indicators.note: about means round, so the gathering surrounds the turned word

parts.note: a bee is a social gathering for work, as in a sewing bee

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word for film is read in reverse

parts.note: a veil is a thin film or covering

explanation.surface: A meeting is held on the financial support for a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' is not a movie but a thin covering; 'the backing of' turns VEIL into LIEV. A bee is a gathering of neighbours for shared work.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold an opinion is to accept it as true, to be convinced of it.

clue.text: Becomes hysterical when unscrupulous lawyer enters an appearance

indicators.note: the legal phrase for turning up in court is used to say the word shows up within the letters

explanation.surface: Someone goes into hysterics when a crooked lawyer turns up in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enters an appearance' is a legal phrase, here saying the answer appears inside becomeS HYSTERical.
explanation.definitionFit: Shyster is American slang for a dishonest, disreputable attorney.
